Strathmore

Strathmore Heavy Industries · Heavy Equipment · North America

From four ERPs and twelve spreadsheets to a single intelligence layer — operationalized in nine weeks.

After a 2023 tier-2 supplier outage cost the company an estimated $14M in lost production, Strathmore set out to consolidate supplier intelligence across four ERPs and 340 buyers. Lattice & Spire was selected after a fourteen-month evaluation; the platform reached production in week nine.

$14.2M Annualized savings within twelve months
73% Tier-2 supplier risk visibility, up from 11%
9 wks From kickoff to production go-live
340 Buyers and planners on a single workspace

The challenge

Strathmore Heavy Industries is a $4.8 billion-revenue manufacturer of construction and material-handling equipment, with eighteen plants across the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The company grew principally through acquisition between 2014 and 2022, absorbing four legacy ERPs — SAP ECC at the Peoria headquarters, Oracle EBS at the acquired Vermillion equipment business, NetSuite at three Mexican plants, and a heavily customized Infor M3 instance at the Canadian forging operations.

Supplier data lived in all four systems, with no single source of truth. The same supplier appeared as "Reichelt Pump Sys GmbH", "Reichelt Pumps", "Reichelt-Pump Systems GMBH", and "RPS" across the network — and that was the easy duplicate to spot. Spend analytics ran in Power BI off a quarterly export. Supplier risk monitoring was a Bloomberg terminal in the corporate procurement office and an ad-hoc email chain to the plant directors. Contract intelligence was a network share organized by year.

In late 2023, a tier-2 supplier in Tianjin halted shipments of cast hydraulic manifolds without notice, costing Strathmore an estimated $14M in lost production over six weeks. The supplier had been visible in procurement's tier-1 records as a sub-supplier to a US-based forging house — but no one had mapped the dependency. After the outage, an internal audit identified eleven additional tier-2 concentrations of similar magnitude. The procurement organization had no operational capacity to monitor them.

Marisol Renteria-Klein, VP Strategic Sourcing, was given a charter and a twelve-month deadline: consolidate supplier intelligence across the four ERPs, build operational tier-2 visibility, and reduce the working-capital impact of long-tail component leadtime drift. She evaluated four platforms across fourteen months.

"We evaluated four platforms across fourteen months. Lattice & Spire was the only one that handled our four-ERP reality without forcing us into a single instance — and the only one whose product team actually understood discrete manufacturing. In nine weeks, we replaced six tools and gave 340 buyers a single pane of glass."
Marisol Renteria-Klein VP Strategic Sourcing, Strathmore Heavy Industries

The solution

Lattice & Spire was selected in February 2025. The deployment was sequenced specifically to avoid a "big bang" migration that would interrupt procurement operations during a planned Q2 production ramp at the Peoria and Saltillo facilities.

The first six weeks focused on ingestion and entity resolution. Lattice & Spire ingested the supplier and PO data from all four ERPs through pre-built bidirectional connectors. The entity-resolution engine collapsed 47,000 supplier records down to 18,300 deduplicated master entities — surfacing 1,800 duplicate-record consolidations in the first pass and another 920 in a second pass that the Strathmore data team manually reviewed.

In parallel, the Lattice & Spire Network Graph enriched the resolved supplier population with multi-tier dependency data drawn from public trade, shipping, and customs sources. By week seven, Strathmore had visibility into 73% of its tier-2 dependencies — including the previously invisible concentration of cast manifolds across three Tianjin suppliers that had caused the 2023 disruption.

Weeks seven through nine focused on workspace rollout. Procurement was the lead workspace, deployed to all 340 category and tactical buyers across the eighteen plants. Risk Radar was configured with category-level alerting rules and routed mitigation tasks into the existing ServiceNow workflow. Contract Vault ingested 14,200 active contracts and surfaced $3.2M in unrealized rebate clauses in the first month. Forecast Engine went live for the long-tail electronic-components category in week ten.

The results

Within twelve months of go-live, Strathmore reported $14.2M in annualized savings attributable to the platform — split roughly across category consolidation ($6.1M), rebate realization ($3.8M), working capital release ($2.7M), and disruption avoidance ($1.6M, estimated).

  • $14.2M annualized savings within the first twelve months of production
  • Tier-2 visibility from 11% to 73% of critical-category supplier dependencies
  • Supplier master consolidation from 47,000 records to 18,300 deduplicated entities
  • $3.8M in unrealized rebates surfaced through Contract Vault in month one
  • Working capital release of $2.7M by aligning safety stock to actual leadtime distributions
  • Disruption response cycle reduced from 14 days to 2.3 days median
  • 340 buyers operating from a single supplier-360 workspace across eighteen plants
  • Six legacy tools retired — including the Bloomberg risk terminal, two contract-management instances, and three Power BI deployments

Implementation details

Deployment timeline
Contract signed Feb 14, 2025 · Kickoff Feb 24 · Data sync complete Apr 1 · Production go-live Apr 28 (week 9.5)
Modules deployed
Supplier 360, Network Graph, Risk Radar, Contract Vault, Insights Hub. Forecast Engine added in month 4 for long-tail electronics.
Integrations connected
SAP ECC (Peoria HQ), Oracle EBS (Vermillion business unit), NetSuite (Mexican operations), Infor M3 (Canadian forging), ServiceNow ITSM, DocuSign CLM, Snowflake (corporate data warehouse), Power BI.
Training hours delivered
340 buyers · 4 hours each role-specific onboarding · 18 super-users (8-hour certification track) · 6 admin users (16-hour certification)
Deployment model
Single-tenant VPC on AWS US-East-2 (Ohio) with cross-region failover to US-West-2 (Oregon). Customer-managed encryption keys via AWS KMS.
Ongoing support model
Premier Enterprise support: dedicated TAM (Customer Success), quarterly executive business reviews, embedded data engineer (1 FTE) for first 6 months.
Internal team
Program sponsor: M. Renteria-Klein (VP Strategic Sourcing) · Program lead: D. Onyemelukwe (Director, Procurement Operations) · Technical lead: Aravind Kalyanaraman (Director, Enterprise Data) · 11 distributed business leads across plants.

Why Lattice & Spire

Strathmore's evaluation considered four platforms across fourteen months — including incumbents the company had used at one or more of the acquired business units. The selection committee documented six reasons for the Lattice & Spire decision:

  • Multi-ERP native architecture — no requirement to consolidate to a single ERP instance as a precondition to deployment
  • Industrial-domain product team — the Lattice & Spire engineering and customer-success organizations understood discrete manufacturing, BOMs, ETO, and aftermarket — without translation
  • Single-tenant VPC option — deployable into Strathmore's AWS account with customer-managed KMS keys, satisfying corporate-IT security requirements
  • Pre-built integrations for all four ERPs in the estate, plus ServiceNow and DocuSign CLM
  • Network Graph multi-tier mapping using public trade, shipping, and customs data — the capability competitors did not match
  • Time-to-value commitment with contractual milestones and credits — production go-live within ten weeks or fee remediation

What's next

Strathmore is expanding the platform footprint in 2026. ESG Tracker is being deployed across the Canadian and Mexican operations ahead of CSRD-aligned reporting obligations that will apply through customer cascades in 2027. Forecast Engine is being extended from the long-tail electronics category to the full hydraulics and powertrain portfolio. The team is also piloting the Lattice & Spire Developer API to embed supplier-360 data into the company's internal product-planning and engineering tools — closing the loop between procurement intelligence and design decisions earlier in the lifecycle.
